footnotes: Pitch is the author’s observation. Bachmann-Geiser 2001: 250 gives pitch simply as “B” (i.e, B-flat).
location: CH-BE, cat. no. 210, inv. no. 24909; ex Kirchgemeinde Pieterlen (acquired by the museum 1935, along with another tenor trombone (****CH-BE, 24910), fragments of yet another tenor trombone (18c2H4), a musettenbass (bass oboe)²  and two liebesfagotten**** (bassoons with spherical bells****).³
signature: “MACHT JOHAN . CARL . KODISCH . IN . NURNB”; master's mark, “ICK” with prancing horse.
pitch: B-natural with slide closed; B-flat perhaps quarter-tone sharp with slide extended approx. 44mm.¹
mouthpiece: not orig; diam. of rim 31.6, rim 5.4, funned-shaped cup with rounded rim; exit 9.2, total length 81.6.
dimensions: : h 1050, l 2700 Dm Röhre 21mm; Dm Stürze 122mm. mp receiver 12, slide exit 9.4/9.8, bo1 10.1/10.35, bo2 10.5, bell sec. 987, slide sec. 1578, overlap 36, le 2529, neck-pipe at bell-bow 12.5, bell-pipe at bell-bow 11.8; bell sec. entry 11.8****[check notes for measurements, check against Bachmann-Geiser.]
literature: Jahrbuch BHM 15 (1935): 137; Wörthmüller 1954: 452ff****; Langwill 1980: 93; Tarr 1984: 449ff; Barclay 1992: 23, 99, 158;**** Waterhouse 1993: 209. Bachmann-Geiser 1998; Bachmann-Geiser 2001: 250-51 (photos).
remarks: Blows freely but sounds airy. Tubular slide stays, decorated with embossed floral-leaf pattern in diagonal stripes; moveable slide-stay telescopic. Bachmann-Geiser 2001 says “middle tubes not original” (“mittlere Röhre nicht original”). Wire ring in slide-bow and bell-bow; saddles engraved with zigzag pattern. Ferrules have embossed floral-leaf pattern and engraved grooves. Flat bell-stay with single eyelet, pin and hinge (pin possibly later manufacture). Ring of embossed shells anterior to garland. Engraved floral ornaments on garland. Sharply flaring bell. Bell at fourth pos. Bell has pronounced terminal flare, a trademark of Kodisch. Nuremberg-style rim wire. Repairs visible in bell sec, 230mm from bell opening; garland was perhaps removed and a new piece inserted underneath. Toothed seam in bell sec. visible at 8 o’clock from player’s perspective****. Instrument very similar to #1701. Bachmann-Geiser 2001 says this trombone,along with #18c2H4 and #1800ca, served the parish of Pieterlen from ca. 1700 to ca. 1770, but this does not accord with the date of either instrument. Examined by the author, June 1999.
